chunks: And from him (Al-Himyari) from Safwan from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Ubayd ibn Zur'ah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed the obligatory Tawaf (of Hajj) but did not pray the two Rak'ahs, then he performed the Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, then he performed the Tawaf of An-Nisa' (the fourth Tawaf) but did not pray the two Rak'ahs, until he mentioned that he was at Al-Abtah. [I asked]: Should he pray four [Rak'ahs]? He said: 'He returns and prays four [Rak'ahs] at the Maqam (of Ibrahim).'

key_terms.بَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ: Between As-Safa and Al-Marwah (the Sa'i ritual)
key_terms.طَوَافَ الْفَرِيضَةِ: Obligatory Tawaf (the first Tawaf of Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to pray the two Rak'ahs after Tawaf before performing Sa'i?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Ubayd ibn Zurara, highlighting the juristic principle that the two Rak'ahs of Tawaf are distinct obligations tied to the specific act of circumambulation rather than the Sa'i itself. The Imam’s directive to return to the Maqam Ibrahim underscores the sanctity of that location as the primary site for these post-Tawaf prayers, ensuring the ritual's completeness even if the pilgrim has already proceeded to the hills of Safa and Marwa.
